## 3060: frechet near nu = 1

Before (`dev/famend-repro.R base frechet`, `repro-base-1.txt`): seed
9031 of `dev/famuni-rev-frechet11.R` (nu0 = 1.1, n = 300) stops at code 0
with the mean intercept at 17.3792, `nu_(Intercept)` (log(nu - 1)) at
-19.138, NaN SEs for both, and only the "Standard errors are not
available ... flat" warning.

The slope in nu alone, which `gev_fit_check()` reads for xi, does not
tell the edge: at seed 9031's stop d logLik / d nu with mu held is
+121.7 (`dev/famend-dbg-frechet.R`, `dbg-frechet.txt`), because mu has to
move with nu. The profile in log(nu - 1), the other two maximized, falls
monotonically toward the edge: -logLik 134.49319865 at -3, 133.77255112
at -6, 133.76387629 at -10, 133.76374240 at -15, 133.76374151 at the
stop and 133.76374149 at -25. So the edge is the supremum.

The rule (`frechet_fit_check()`, `frechet_ridge_gain()` in
`R/families-extreme.R`): where a scalar nu is within 1e-3 of 1, move
log(nu - 1) three e-folds toward 1 and the intercept of log(mu) by the
change in `lgamma(1 - 1/nu)`, which holds the scale; if the
log-likelihood does not fall, warn (class `frmtmb_frechet_nu_edge`). The
objective is put back at the stop afterwards. A predicted nu, or a mu
without a log link or an intercept, gets a message
(`frmtmb_frechet_nu_near_edge`) naming the distance only.

After (`repro-lane-gevgrad2.txt`): seed 9031 warns "frechet: nu ran to 1
+ 4.88e-09, the edge at nu = 1, and the likelihood does not fall toward
it (it changes by 1.37e-08 ...)". The warning marks the SE warning as
explained, so the "flat" warning is not repeated.

Guard absent (`dev/famend-probe-frechet.R`, lane logs
`frechet-n300-lane.txt` and `frechet-near-lane.txt`, summary below):
every interior maximum loses likelihood toward the edge, and the
largest such "gain" is -0.000959, at nu - 1 = 0.002 (seed 9039). The
edge fits gain 1.0e-8 to 3.4e-7. No interior maximum within 1e-3 of 1
was found: at n = 300 the closest was 0.002, and the SE of nu there
puts an interior maximum that close out of reach of any realistic n.

## 3067: GEV gradient NaN far below the location

WITHDRAWN FIX: the cap of 500 described below made a nested-quadrature
GEV fit read logLik Inf under OpenBLAS (review F1). The fix round
restored the cap of 700 and removed the band in `gev_parts()`
instead; see "Fix round", F1. The measurements of 0.82.0 below stand.

Before (`dev/famend-repro.R base gevgrad`, `repro-base-1.txt`): an
outside row, sigma 1, x stepped by 0.01 from just below the support to
60 units further: 80 of 6000 points have a non-finite gradient at each
of xi 0.06, 0.3 and 1, all at x in [-20.26, -19.47]; the Hessian is
non-finite at 9 or 10 of 600 probed points. The cause: `gev_parts()`
clamps an outside row at z = -1 + 1e-15, where `log1p_ratio()` has a
slope of about 1e15; the reverse sweep forms exp(-h) (up to exp(700)
under the old cap) times that slope before the clamp's zero derivative
meets it, which overflows to Inf, and Inf * 0 is NaN.

Fix: `exp_neg_capped(w, cap)`; the GEV's density and CDF call it with
cap 500, the Frechet keeps 700. At 500 the third derivative, about
exp(500) 1e45, fits in a double. A first version moved both families
to 500, and `test-families-extreme.R` ("the Frechet density is Stan's")
failed: it pins the Frechet's tape log density exact to z = 1e270, past
w = -500. The Frechet has no clamp in its chain and no NaN band (0 of
401 rows with log y from -166.7 to -300, nu = 3, base and lane), so it
keeps 700. A GEV row inside its support reaches w = -500 only where its
log density is below -1e217.

After (`repro-lane-gevgrad2.txt`): 0 of 6000 non-finite gradients and
0 of 600 non-finite Hessians at each xi.

## 3075: GEV with xi below -0.5

Before (`repro-base-1.txt`, data of `dev/boundfam-repro.R` case gev,
seed 4, n = 300): xi0 -0.63, -0.7, -0.89 fit at xi -0.6628, -0.7362,
-0.9361 with code 0, finite SEs and no condition.

After (`repro-lane-1.txt`): each gets the message "gen_extreme_value:
xi is -0.6628338, below -0.5. There the maximum of the likelihood is not
regular (Smith, 1985): the standard errors of mu, sigma and xi are not
asymptotically normal ... confint(method = "profile") gives an interval
that does not use them" (class `frmtmb_gev_xi_nonregular`). Guard
absent: xi0 -0.3 and -0.45 (fitted -0.313, -0.473) get nothing. A
message, not a warning: a true xi in that range is a correct model. A
xi held at a constant gets it too: the non-regularity is in the
support's end, mu - sigma / xi.

nb2 both get "Boundary fit: shape_(Intercept) [sigma_(Intercept)] is at

-549.3707295947 and -549.3707322512; seed 1 (a real maximum) agrees to

## 2750: the cs() ordinal-mixture wall

Before and after on `dev/optima-csmix-wall.R`'s 20 data sets
(`dev/famend-repro.R csmix`; summary below). The 18 code-1 fits each
have a row whose own category is 1.4e-15 to 2.3e-13 wide on the link
scale; none was named on base. On the lane all 18 get, in
`mixture_ord_degenerate_check()`'s warning, "component 1 (a cs() effect
has closed a category: on row 66 the two thresholds of the observed
category are 1.4e-14 apart on the link scale, and past that they cross,
where the category's probability would be negative)" (seed 3). The 2
converged fits (narrowest category 0.509 and 0.893) get nothing. The
cut is 1e-8. `mixture_ord_degeneracy()` gains columns `closed` and
`closed_row`; `mixture_ord_start_class()` does not read them, so the
multi-start paths do not change.

## 3560: a positive-support prior on a coefficient that starts at 0

The original construction (`dev/fuzzfix-rev-r2-edges.R`) is refused by
the weights check since 0.82.0 ("The weighted likelihood of this model
has no maximum"), with or without the prior and with `lb = 0`, which
is the weights check's own call. Without the weights and `(1 | obs)`
the defect is there (`dev/famend-probe-gprior.R`, `gprior-base.txt`):
`gamma(2, 1)` and `lognormal(0, 1)` on the coefficients of
`shape ~ 0 + fac` leave the fit at its start, betad 0 0, objective Inf,
code 0 (code 1 with `lb = 0`), with only the gradient warning. The
start of 0 is where those densities are 0. From a start of 1 the fit
converges (objective 124.6379).

Fix: `prior_start_inside()` (R/priors.R) moves a start where the
prior's log density is not finite to a point well inside the support
(the gamma's and exponential's mean, the lognormal's median, the
inverse gamma's mode, the beta's mean, the uniform's midpoint), on the
internal, natural and sd scales; one call in `make_start()` (R/fit.R).
A start with a positive density, a parameter held at a constant, and a
caller's `start` are left as they are.

After (`gprior-lane.txt`): no lb, lb = 0 and a start of 1 all reach
objective 124.6379 at betad 0.601504 0.925724; lognormal reaches
123.8405; shape 0.4 data with lb = 0 reach 128.1815. The guard-absent
arms (exponential(1), normal(0, 1), gaussian with gamma on b of mu)
are unchanged to every printed digit.

## 3618: OSA on a censored count

Before (`dev/famend-osa.R base`, `osa-base.txt`): every censored count
refused ("not supported on a cens() fit with a discrete family").

The window an uncensored row lies in is `(lo, hi]` for counts and
continuous responses alike, by brms's reading of a discrete bound (left
at k is Y <= k, right at k is Y > k). On the "cdf" route the tails are
`F(y) - F(lo)` and `F(hi) - F(y)`, not divided by the window's mass:
TMB divides each row's mass and lower tail by the sum of its tails,
which is that mass, while the density term stays the fitted one that
later rows condition on. The blocks of the "cdf" route hold the
uncensored rows, each conditioned on every censored row too, as the one
call is. `oneStepGeneric` sums over `lo + 1, ..., hi`.

After (`osa-lane.txt`, `osa-lane-both.txt`):

- poisson right-censored at 4 (the triage's construction): censored
  rows NA 18 of 18, uncensored finite 82 of 82, max relative |r - exact
  randomized PIT| 9.21e-15;
- window (1, 6], n = 300: poisson 1.95e-14 (211 of 211 rows in their own
  step), negbinomial 1.13e-13 (182 of 182), binomial 1.53e-13 (199 of
  199), zero-inflated poisson 2.5e-14 (167 of 167);
- poisson `(1 | g)`, 30 groups of 10, 126 censored: "cdf" against
  oneStepGeneric max |diff| 0.00145, median 8.91e-5 (two Laplace
  routes); row blocks against one call 7.19e-11; KS p 0.0906; times
  18.3 s, 42.7 s and 74.9 s;
- a censored gaussian, [-0.5, 2.5]: the default oneStepGeneric 7.05e-15
  and "cdf" 5.54e-15 from the exact PIT.

## 5726: fractional weights on a continuous response

Before (`osa-base.txt`): gaussian, 36 rows of weight in (0, 1): NA on
all 36 with the `frmtmb_osa_weight` warning; Gamma the same on 34.

After (`osa-lane.txt`): gaussian, NA 0, max relative |r - qnorm(F(y))|
2.32e-15 on the fractional rows (1.58e-15 on the others); Gamma 34 of 34
finite, 6.38e-15 from the exact; weight-0 rows NA 3 of 3; poisson keeps
NA on 36 of 36 with the warning; gaussian `(1 | g)`, 40 groups, every
second row weight 0.5: 200 of 200 finite, mean 0.022, sd 0.978, KS p
0.415 (weight-1 rows 0.359). Rule: on the "cdf" route a continuous
row's residual reads its tails alone, which below weight 1 carry no
copy of the density, so it is the CDF of a fresh copy given the rows
before it (the osa review's item 8).

## 5722: pbeta() for the binomial and negative binomial pairs

`dev/famend-cost.R base` (`cost-base.txt`), one value-and-gradient sweep
of 20,000 rows, best of 5 rounds of 20: `RTMB::ppois()` 5.00 ms,
`poisson_cdf_log()` both tails 312.5 ms, `binomial_cdf_log()` 984.5 ms,
`RTMB::pbeta()` both tails logged 78.0 ms, `nbinom_cdf_log()` 937.5 ms.
So pbeta is 12.6 times cheaper per sweep. But its log tails: max error
1.6e-19 at size 20, 6.7e-16 at 200, and at size 2000 0.000792 with 3 of
7 points non-finite; and swapped into the one-step tape of a binomial
`(1 | g)` fit of 800 rows (this process only, `assignInNamespace()`),
704 of 800 residuals were non-finite (19.4 s as built, 7.0 s swapped).
For the negative binomial the shape is a parameter, where
`RTMB::pbeta()`'s derivative is 0 at an integer shape
(`student_cdf_log()`'s documentation). Not adopted; the item is closed
with these numbers.

## 3580: the cost of a CDF pair

`dev/famend-cost-pois.R`, rows right-censored at 5, 20,000 rows:
`poisson_cdf_log()`'s survivor 262.5 ms per sweep on base against 37.5
ms for its upper sum written as one Horner sweep of products. The
lane replaces the 39 `logspace_add()` terms of the upper sum by that
sweep (`R/families-cdf.R`); the lower sum and the blend stay.

`dev/famend-pois-check.R` (`pois-check.txt`), counts 1 to 30 by means
1e-3 to 160 (2400 points): new against 0.82.0's form max relative 5.69e-14
(lF) and 1.01e-15 (lS); against `stats::ppois(log.p = TRUE)` 3.34e-12
and 4.74e-13 for both forms; where the sweep holds mu at q + 41, P(Y <=
q) is at most 3.24e-8, so that arm is weighted 0 there; first, second
and third derivatives in log(mu) finite at 2400 of 2400 points, max
relative difference from 0.82.0's 5.67e-10.

After (`cost-pois-lane.txt`): the survivor 79.5 ms per sweep (3.3
times faster). `dev/famend-quadmem.R` (the release review's
construction, seed 20261021, 1440 rows, `(1 | g)`, right-censored at 5,
one fit per process, interleaved runs; time measures load):

| arm | Laplace | quadrature |
|---|---|---|
| base (`quadmem-base2.txt`) | 7.2 s, 495 MB | 64.3 s, 3380 MB |
| lane (`quadmem-lane.txt`) | 4.2 s, 454 MB | 33.4 s, 2773 MB |

logLik equal to the printed six decimals in both arms (-2377.539366,
-2376.379191). 0.72.0 had 2.3 s and 495 MB under quadrature
(the backlog's table), so the rest is filed as a new LOW item.

## Existing tests the change reaches

The one-file run found two, both pinning what this lane changes:

- `test-linpred-layers.R` ("several location predictors stack, and
  cs() adds its thresholds"): its `mixture(cumulative(), cumulative())`
  fit with `cs(z)` stops at false convergence (the test already allows
  that warning), with a row's category 2.3e-14 wide; the new wall
  warning escaped (warn = 1). Added "cs() effect has closed a category"
  to its allowed list, with a comment. 83 pass, 0 warn after.
- `test-prior-table-brms.R` ("zero-density ends get no box; an Inf stop
  is not converged"): `beta(2, 2)` on a slope the data put below 0.
  `dev/famend-probe-beta22.R` (`beta22-base.txt`, `beta22-lane.txt`):
  with no bound, base fails ("optimizer failed ... NA/NaN gradient
  evaluation") and the lane reaches objective 129.8616523, z 0.00682207,
  as `lb = 1e-8` does on both; in the closed box [0, 1] base stops at
  z = 0 with the objective Inf and code 1, the lane reaches the same
  mode. The test asserted the old failures (4 failures on the lane).
  Rewritten: both arms now must reach `lb = 1e-8`'s objective, and the
  final-stop guard (owner priors2) is kept with a caller's start on 0,
  `start = list(beta = c(1, 0))`, which still stops at Inf with code 1
  on both builds. 99 pass after. With a caller's start on 0 and NO
  bound both builds stop at code 0 with the objective Inf: filed LOW.

and `0.3.32 lapack` both built (`famend-out/openblas-026.txt`,

### F1 (HIGH): the GEV cap

The cap is back at `exp(700)`, the block of `exp_neg_capped()` identical
to 0.82.0's. The NaN band is removed at its source instead: in
`gev_parts()` the ratio `log1p(zc) / zc` is read through
`ad_min(., gev_ratio_top)`, a constant 64 ulps below the ratio at the
clamp `zc = -1 + 1e-15`. An outside row sits at the clamp, so it reads
the constant, and the reverse sweep multiplies the adjoint by the zero
derivative before the clamp's 1e15 slope can meet it. The next `zc`
above the clamp has a ratio 0.1 lower, so no other row reads it.

`dev/famend-gevbit.R` (`famend-out/gevbit-ref.txt`), this build's
`gev_parts()` against 0.82.0's in one process:

```text

OUTSIDE xi 0.001: 6000 rows; non-finite gradient 0, Hessian 0 (this build); 0.82.0's gev_parts, every 5th row: 0 of 1200
OUTSIDE xi  0.01: 6000 rows; non-finite gradient 0, Hessian 0 (this build); 0.82.0's gev_parts, every 5th row: 0 of 1200
```

The inside rows are xi -0.9 to 10, the three slots (density, CDF, log
survivor), 399 rows across the support plus rows 1e-13, 1e-10 and 1e-6
inside each finite end. The 10 Hessians per xi (`dev/famend-gevhess.R`,

### test-prior-table-brms.R

Added: the no-bound fit runs with no finite bound on z
(`fit$cache$bounds`), so the moved start, not a box, reaches the mode.
101 pass on every arm.

Merge with priors2 (its tree, read only): priors2 rewrote the same
test ("zero-density ends get no box; a bound there reaches the mode").
It keeps 0.82.0's "with no bound it ... fails loudly" `expect_error()`
and asserts that `sp(lb = 0, ub = 1)` reaches m8's objective through
`open_end_coords()`. On the merged build the `expect_error()` fails,
because `prior_start_inside()` moves the start and the fit converges.
Resolution: take priors2's test, and replace its block

```r
  # with no bound it is not boxed: the fit fails as before, loudly,
  # rather than stop at the end
  expect_error(allow_warnings(frm(yneg ~ z, data = d, prior = sp()),
                              c(w, "NA/NaN function evaluation")),
               "optimizer failed", class = "frmtmb_error")
```

with famend's

```r
  # with no bound, the start the slope's least squares gives (below 0,
  # where the density is 0) moves inside the support, and the mode is
  # found with no box on z
  nb <- allow_warnings(frm(yneg ~ z, data = d, prior = sp()), w)
  expect_identical(nb$opt$convergence, 0L)
  expect_lte(abs(nb$opt$objective - m8$opt$objective),
             1e-8 * abs(m8$opt$objective))
  iz <- which(frmtmb:::outer_par_names(nb) == "z")
  expect_length(iz, 1L)
  expect_false(any(is.finite(c(nb$cache$bounds$lower[iz],
                               nb$cache$bounds$upper[iz]))))
```

and keep priors2's `at0` block (the closed box reaches the mode; on
famend's build it does too, through the moved start). Drop famend's
caller-start `at0` (code 1, objective Inf): beside priors2's open chart
it is not known to hold, and the final-stop guard it pins is priors2's
to test. Run the merged file under reference and ob before release.

## Fix round 2 (short check dev/reviews/2026-11-13-famend-short.md, F1)

### F1: the GEV band at xi 0.44 to 0.84

Cause (the short check's): `zc = ad_max(z + out, cl)`, `cl = -1 + 1e-15`,
`out = ad_pos(cl - z)`. Where `out` is in [8, 16) its rounding leaves
`z + out` at `-1 + 2^-49`, 7 ulps above the clamp; the second clamp
does not lift it, the ratio there (33.96) is below `gev_ratio_top`, so
the `ad_min()` of round 1 passes its slope (about 5.6e14) and the
adjoint overflows.

Change (`R/families-extreme.R`, `gev_parts()`): after 0.82.0's
`r = ad_max(z + out, cl)`, subtract the excess `ex = r - cl` through
`ad_pos(ex) - ad_pos(ex - out)`. On an outside row `ex` is exact (r is
near cl) and below `out`, so `zc` is `cl` to the bit; on an inside row
`out` is 0 and the two `ad_pos()` terms are the same value, so `zc` is
`z`. A first form, `ad_max(r - ad_min(r - cl, out), cl)`, had the same
values but sent an inside row's adjoint through one `ad_pos()` of a
positive argument, `2 * fl(0.5 A)`, which is not `A` for an odd
subnormal `A`: 8 of 19287 inside rows x slots of `famend-gevbit.R` and
2 of 4422 of `famend-short-gevclamp.R` differed from 0.82.0
(`dev/famend-fix2-xi0diff.R` on that build, its log since overwritten
by the kept build's, which lists no row: xi -1e-4 lcdf at x 694.5 and
xi 0 lcdf at x -6.6, gradient and Hessian entries from 1e-313 to
1e-302, equal to 6 digits; the 8 gevbit rows were not inspected). In
the kept form the two positive-argument `ad_pos()` terms
take `-A` and `+A` and cancel exactly. The last clamp of the first form
is not needed: `dev/famend-fix2-replay.R` (`fix2-replay.txt`), the
arithmetic on doubles:

```text
OUTSIDE rows 3000401: zc != clamp, old 523538 (above 523538, below 0), new 0
  of them cl - z in [8, 16): 118997 rows, old above the clamp 118997, new 0
  |z| > 2^52: 434644 rows, old zc range [-1, 0], new zc != clamp 0
FAR OUTSIDE |z| 1e15 to 1e40, 1000000 rows: zc != clamp, old 961816 (zc 0: 961816), new 0
INSIDE rows 3000400: zc != z, old 0, new 0; new != old 0
```

(0.82.0 also put outside rows past `|z|` 1e16 at `zc = 0`, so `l = 0`;
they are now on the clamp too.)
